title: Runtime Surge Attenuator and Fallback Conductor: adaptive per-entity breakers and confidence-weighted shedding
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight, adaptive circuit/breaker layer (Surge Attenuator) plus a Fallback Conductor orchestrator that applies safe, observable degradations per dependency/model/tenant. The design purposefully avoids global hard-trips: breakers are soft-tripping, confidence-weighted, and scoped to an entity (tenant/model/region/dependency) to preserve noisy-neighbor isolation and predictable SLOs.

Key features: 
- Multi-dimensional trip signals: combined error-rate (5m and 1h), P99 latency spike ratio, queue-depth pressure, and token-usage budget exhaustion.
- Soft-trip windowing: a breaker moves through states (ok -> strained -> attenuate -> soft-open) with hysteresis derived from SLO slack and recent rollback success.
- Confidence-weighted shedding: when capacity is constrained, requests carry an importance score (customer tier + request annotations + token budget). The conductor preferentially routes/accepts higher-confidence requests.
- Per-entity fallback paths: for a tripped model dependency, orchestrate ordered fallbacks: (1) local model variant (quantized or lower-context), (2) regional replica, (3) cached response / prefix-KV replay, (4) lightweight heuristic response (safe deny) with transparent headers and metrics.
- Safe-mode checks: before promoting a fallback we run a quick golden-set verification for a sampled subset (latency and semantic sanity) to prevent silent quality regressions.
- Multi-region failover policy: automatic regional candidate selection by routing score, with circuit-awareness (avoid failover loops) and capacity tagging to prefer dedicated pools for enterprise tenants.
- Observability: per-trip root cause tags, snapshot of top-5 contributing metrics, and an auto-created incident draft when an entity crosses a critical soft-trip threshold for >2min.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Complexity vs determinism: chose deterministic simple scoring over a fully learned policy to keep operator predictability and safety.
- Per-request scoring adds header/SDK changes: mitigated with backwards-compatible defaults and server-side heuristics for legacy clients.
- Golden-set checks increase overhead: limited to 1% sampling and async verification.

Acceptance criteria: 
- New breaker state machine implemented in runtime with feature flag.
- Fallback Conductor can execute ordered fallbacks with documented audit trail in Console.
- No regression in median latency (<=1% delta) for a 10k qps canary.
- End-to-end chaos test (region outage + synthetic traffic spike) shows graceful degradation for P99 within SLO slack and <=5% failed high-tier requests.

Links: design doc: https://confluence.company/reliability/surge-attenuator-design, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821, load-test dashboard: https://grafana.company/d/rt/surge-80512
comments: 2026-02-10 Sofia Martinez: Triage - high priority after two customer incidents where single-model saturation caused cross-tenant degradation. Proposing per-entity soft-trip to lower blast radius.

2026-03-07 Evan Li (Design): Mockups for Console UI posted. Emphasize clear labels: 'soft-attenuated' vs 'hard-open'. Keep manual override gated to SRE and tenant owners.
